overall: The AG found the committee violated the OML by approving its March 19 and April 2 minutes more than 30 days later without good cause, but found the minutes were sufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the committee failed to approve its March 19 meeting minutes in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: We conclude that the Committee did not provide good cause for the delay and therefore it violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve the minutes in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the committee failed to approve its April 2 meeting minutes in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: Yet, the Committee reviewed and approved the March 19 minutes at its April 23 meeting, 35 days later; and reviewed and approved the April 2 minutes at its May 21 meeting, 49 days later.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the March 19 minutes did not adequately summarize the Finance Subcommittee update.
allegations.key_passage: While the approved minutes from the March 19 meeting do not specifically include reference to each audit that the Finance Subcommittee reviewed, they otherwise offer a concise summary of the subcommittee’s ongoing projects.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the March 26 minutes did not adequately summarize the Superintendent's update on the Assistant Superintendent search.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, we find that the approved minutes from the March 26 meeting also offer a concise summary, even though they do not specifically reference the date by which the Superintendent would submit a named candidate to the Committee.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements (approve minutes in a timely manner).
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
